text: The book claims that strong induction is strictly more powerful than ordinary mathematical induction: some statements provable by strong induction cannot be proved by ordinary induction.
explanation: False. The book states that strong induction is logically equivalent to ordinary induction — 'two names for the same principle.' Strong induction (assuming P(0),...,P(k)) is merely more convenient when P(k+1) depends on earlier cases, not more powerful; anything provable one way is provable the other.
